## codegraph
# Codegraph — code intelligence over an indexed knowledge graph

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of every symbol, edge, and file in
the workspace — pre-computed structure you would otherwise re-derive by
reading files (cached intelligence: thousands of parse/trace decisions you
don't pay to re-reason each run). Reads are sub-millisecond; the index lags
writes by ~1s through the file watcher. Reach for it BEFORE *and* while
writing or editing code — not just for questions: one call returns the
verbatim source PLUS who calls it and what it affects, so you edit with the
blast radius in view. More accurate context, in far fewer tokens and
round-trips than reading files yourself.

## One tool: codegraph_explore — use it instead of reading files

There is a single tool, `codegraph_explore`, and it is Read-equivalent. It
takes either a natural-language question or a bag of symbol/file names and
returns the **verbatim, line-numbered source** of the relevant symbols
grouped by file — the same `<n>\t<line>` shape `Read` gives you, safe to
`Edit` from — PLUS the call path among them (including dynamic-dispatch hops
like callbacks, React re-render, and JSX children that grep can't follow) and
a blast-radius summary of what depends on them.

Whether you're answering "how does X work" or implementing a change (fixing a
bug, adding a feature), call `codegraph_explore` before you Read. ONE call
usually answers the whole question. Codegraph IS the pre-built search index —
so running your own grep + read loop, or delegating the lookup to a separate
file-reading sub-task/agent, repeats work codegraph already did and costs more
for the same answer. A direct codegraph answer is typically one to a few
calls; a grep/read exploration is dozens.

## How to query

- **Almost any question — "how does X work", architecture, a bug, "what/where is X", or surveying an area** → `codegraph_explore` with a natural-language question or the relevant names. ONE capped call returns the verbatim source grouped by file; most often the ONLY call y… [truncated]

68	// Register adds a job to the scheduler.

70	func (s *Scheduler) Register(job *Job) error {
71		if job == nil {
72			return errors.New("job cannot be nil")
73		}
74	
75		if err := job.Validate(); err != nil {
76			return errors.Wrap(err, "invalid job")
77		}
78	
79		s.jobsMu.Lock()
80		defer s.jobsMu.Unlock()
81	
82		if _, exists := s.jobs[job.Name]; exists {
83			return errors.Errorf("job with name %q already registered", job.Name)
84		}

88	}

90	// Start begins executing scheduled jobs.
91	func (s *Scheduler) Start() error {
92		s.runningMu.Lock()
93		defer s.runningMu.Unlock()
94	
95		if s.running {
96			return errors.New("scheduler already running")
97		}
98	
99		s.jobsMu.RLock()
100		defer s.jobsMu.RUnlock()
101	
102		// Parse and schedule all jobs
103		for _, rj := range s.jobs {
104			schedule, err := ParseCronExpression(rj.job.Schedule)
105			if err != nil {
106				return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to parse schedule for job %q", rj.job.Name)
107			}
108	
109			ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
110			rj.cancelFn = cancel
111	
112			s.wg.Add(1)
113			go s.runJobWithSchedule(ctx, rj, schedule)
114		}
115	
116		s.running = true
117		return nil
118	}

120	// runJobWithSchedule executes a job according to its cron schedule.
121	func (s *Scheduler) runJobWithSchedule(ctx context.Context, rj *registeredJob, schedule *Schedule) {
122		defer s.wg.Done()
123	
124		// Apply middleware to handler
125		handler := rj.job.Handler
126		if s.middleware != nil {
127			handler = s.middleware(handler)
128		}
129	
130		for {
131			// Calculate next run time
132			now := time.Now()
133			if rj.job.Timezone != "" {
134				loc, err := time.LoadLocation(rj.job.Timezone)
135				if err == nil {
136					now = now.In(loc)
137				}
138			} else if s.timezone != nil {
139				now = now.In(s.timezone)
140			}
141	
142			next := schedule.Next(now)
143			duration := time.Until(next)
144	
145			timer := time.NewTimer(duration)
146	
147			select {
148			case <-timer.C:
149				// Add job name to context and execute
150				jobCtx := withJobName(ctx, rj.job.Name)
151				if err := handler(jobCtx); err != nil {
152					// Error already handled by middleware (if any)
153					_ = err
154				}
155			case <-ctx.Done():
156				// Stop the timer to prevent it from firing. The timer will be garbage collected.
157				timer.Stop()
158				return
159			case <-s.stopCh:
160				// Stop the timer to prevent it from firing. The timer will be garbage collected.
161				timer.Stop()
162				return
163			}
164		}
165	}

167	// Stop gracefully shuts down the scheduler.
168	// It waits for all running jobs to complete or until the context is canceled.
169	func (s *Scheduler) Stop(ctx context.Context) error {
170		s.runningMu.Lock()
171		if !s.running {
172			s.runningMu.Unlock()
173			return errors.New("scheduler not running")
174		}
175		s.running = false
176		s.runningMu.Unlock()
177	
178		// Cancel all job contexts
179		s.jobsMu.RLock()
180		for _, rj := range s.jobs {
181			if rj.cancelFn != nil {
182				rj.cancelFn()
183			}
184		}
185		s.jobsMu.RUnlock()
186	
187		// Signal stop and wait for jobs to finish
188		close(s.stopCh)
189	
190		done := make(chan struct{})
191		go func() {
192			s.wg.Wait()
193			close(done)
194		}()
195	
196		select {
197		case <-done:
198			return nil
199		case <-ctx.Done():
200			return ctx.Err()
201		}

49		if err != nil {

51		}
52	
53		s3StorageType := storepb.AttachmentStorageType_S3
54		// Limit attachments to a reasonable batch size
55		const batchSize = 100
56		offset := 0
57	
58		for {
59			limit := batchSize
60			attachments, err := r.Store.ListAttachments(ctx, &store.FindAttachment{
61				GetBlob:     false,
62				StorageType: &s3StorageType,
63				Limit:       &limit,
64				Offset:      &offset,
65			})
66			if err != nil {
67				slog.Error("Failed to list attachments for presigning", "error", err)
68				return
69			}
70	
71			// Break if no more attachments
72			if len(attachments) == 0 {
73				break
74			}
75	
76			// Process batch of attachments
77			presignCount := 0
78			for _, attachment := range attachments {
79				payload := cloneAttachmentPayload(attachment.Payload)
80				s3ObjectPayload := payload.GetS3Object()
81				if s3ObjectPayload == nil {
82					continue
83				}
84	
85				if s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime != nil {
86					// Skip if the presigned URL is still valid for the next 4 days.
87					// The expiration time is set to 5 days.
88					if time.Now().Before(s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime.AsTime().Add(4 * 24 * time.Hour)) {
89						continue
90					}
91				}
92	
93				s3Config := instanceStorageSetting.GetS3Config()
94				if s3ObjectPayload.S3Config != nil {
95					s3Config = s3ObjectPayload.S3Config
96				}
97				if s3Config == nil {
98					slog.Error("S3 config is not found")
99					continue
100				}
101	
102				s3Client, err := s3.NewClient(ctx, s3Config)
103				if err != nil {
104					slog.Error("Failed to create S3 client", "error", err)
105					continue
106				}
107	
108				presignURL, err := s3Client.PresignGetObject(ctx, s3ObjectPayload.Key)
109				if err != nil {
110					slog.Error("Failed to presign URL", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
111					continue
112				}
113	
114				s3ObjectPayload.S3Config = s3Config
115				s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime = timestamppb.New(time.Now())
116				if err := r.Store.UpdateAttachment(ctx, &store.UpdateAttachment{
117					ID:        attachment.ID,
118					Reference: &presignURL,
119					Payload:   payload,
120				}); err != nil {

122					continue

34	func handleSSE(c *echo.Context, hub *SSEHub, authenticator *auth.Authenticator) error {
35		// Authenticate the request.
36		authHeader := c.Request().Header.Get("Authorization")
37		result := authenticator.Authenticate(c.Request().Context(), authHeader)
38		if result == nil {
39			return c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "authentication required"})
40		}
41		userID, role := getSSEClientIdentity(result)
42		if userID == 0 {
43			return c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "authentication required"})
44		}
45	
46		// Set SSE headers.
47		w := c.Response()
48		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
49		w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
50		w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")
51		w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no") // Disable nginx buffering
52		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
53	
54		// Flush headers immediately.
55		if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
56			f.Flush()
57		}
58	
59		// Subscribe to the hub.
60		client := hub.Subscribe(userID, role)
61		defer hub.Unsubscribe(client)
62	
63		// Create a ticker for heartbeat pings.
64		heartbeat := time.NewTicker(sseHeartbeatInterval)
65		defer heartbeat.Stop()
66	
67		ctx := c.Request().Context()
68	
69		slog.Debug("SSE client connected", "userID", userID)
70	
71		// Send an initial comment so clients and dev proxies observe the stream
72		// immediately instead of waiting for the first heartbeat or data event.
73		if _, err := fmt.Fprint(w, ": connected\n\n"); err != nil {
74			return nil
75		}
76		if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
77			f.Flush()
78		}
79	
80		for {
81			select {
82			case <-ctx.Done():
83				// Client disconnected.
84				slog.Debug("SSE client disconnected", "userID", userID)
85				return nil
86	
87			case data, ok := <-client.events:
88				if !ok {
89					// Channel closed, client was unsubscribed.
90					return nil
91				}
92				// Write SSE event.
93				if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %s\n\n", data); err != nil {
94					return nil
95				}
96				if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
97					f.Flush()
98				}
99	
100			case <-heartbeat.C:
101				// Send a heartbeat comment to keep the connection alive.
102				if _, err := fmt.Fprint(w, ": heartbeat\n\n"); err != nil {
103					return nil
104				}

47	func (r *Runner) CheckAndPresign(ctx context.Context) {
48		instanceStorageSetting, err := r.Store.GetInstanceStorageSetting(ctx)
49		if err != nil {
50			return
51		}
52	
53		s3StorageType := storepb.AttachmentStorageType_S3
54		// Limit attachments to a reasonable batch size
55		const batchSize = 100
56		offset := 0
57	
58		for {
59			limit := batchSize
60			attachments, err := r.Store.ListAttachments(ctx, &store.FindAttachment{
61				GetBlob:     false,
62				StorageType: &s3StorageType,
63				Limit:       &limit,
64				Offset:      &offset,
65			})
66			if err != nil {
67				slog.Error("Failed to list attachments for presigning", "error", err)
68				return
69			}
70	
71			// Break if no more attachments
72			if len(attachments) == 0 {
73				break
74			}
75	
76			// Process batch of attachments
77			presignCount := 0
78			for _, attachment := range attachments {
79				payload := cloneAttachmentPayload(attachment.Payload)
80				s3ObjectPayload := payload.GetS3Object()
81				if s3ObjectPayload == nil {
82					continue
83				}
84	
85				if s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime != nil {
86					// Skip if the presigned URL is still valid for the next 4 days.
87					// The expiration time is set to 5 days.
88					if time.Now().Before(s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime.AsTime().Add(4 * 24 * time.Hour)) {
89						continue
90					}
91				}
92	
93				s3Config := instanceStorageSetting.GetS3Config()
94				if s3ObjectPayload.S3Config != nil {
95					s3Config = s3ObjectPayload.S3Config
96				}
97				if s3Config == nil {
98					slog.Error("S3 config is not found")
99					continue
100				}
101	
102				s3Client, err := s3.NewClient(ctx, s3Config)
103				if err != nil {
104					slog.Error("Failed to create S3 client", "error", err)
105					continue
106				}
107	
108				presignURL, err := s3Client.PresignGetObject(ctx, s3ObjectPayload.Key)
109				if err != nil {
110					slog.Error("Failed to presign URL", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
111					continue
112				}
113	
114				s3ObjectPayload.S3Config = s3Config
115				s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime = timestamppb.New(time.Now())
116				if err := r.Store.UpdateAttachment(ctx, &store.UpdateAttachment{
117					ID:        attachment.ID,
118					Reference: &presignURL,
119					Payload:   payload,
120				}); err != nil {
121					slog.Error("Failed to update attachment", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
122					continue
123				}
124				presignCount++
125			}
126	
127			slog.Info("Presigned batch of S3 attachments", "batchSize", len(attachments), "presigned", presignCount)
128	
129			// Move to next batch
130			offset += len(attachments)
131		}
132	}

32	// handleSSE handles the SSE connection for live memo refresh.
33	// Authentication is done via Bearer token in the Authorization header.
34	func handleSSE(c *echo.Context, hub *SSEHub, authenticator *auth.Authenticator) error {
35		// Authenticate the request.
36		authHeader := c.Request().Header.Get("Authorization")
37		result := authenticator.Authenticate(c.Request().Context(), authHeader)
38		if result == nil {
39			return c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "authentication required"})
40		}
41		userID, role := getSSEClientIdentity(result)
42		if userID == 0 {
43			return c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "authentication required"})
44		}
45	
46		// Set SSE headers.
47		w := c.Response()
48		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
49		w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
50		w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")
51		w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no") // Disable nginx buffering
52		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
53	
54		// Flush headers immediately.
55		if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
56			f.Flush()
57		}
58	
59		// Subscribe to the hub.
60		client := hub.Subscribe(userID, role)
61		defer hub.Unsubscribe(client)
62	
63		// Create a ticker for heartbeat pings.
64		heartbeat := time.NewTicker(sseHeartbeatInterval)
65		defer heartbeat.Stop()
66	
67		ctx := c.Request().Context()
68	
69		slog.Debug("SSE client connected", "userID", userID)
70	
71		// Send an initial comment so clients and dev proxies observe the stream
72		// immediately instead of waiting for the first heartbeat or data event.
73		if _, err := fmt.Fprint(w, ": connected\n\n"); err != nil {
74			return nil
75		}
76		if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
77			f.Flush()
78		}
79	
80		for {
81			select {
82			case <-ctx.Done():
83				// Client disconnected.
84				slog.Debug("SSE client disconnected", "userID", userID)
85				return nil
86	
87			case data, ok := <-client.events:
88				if !ok {
89					// Channel closed, client was unsubscribed.
90					return nil
91				}
92				// Write SSE event.
93				if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %s\n\n", data); err != nil {
94					return nil
95				}
96				if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
97					f.Flush()
98				}
99	
100			case <-heartbeat.C:
101				// Send a heartbeat comment to keep the connection alive.
102				if _, err := fmt.Fprint(w, ": heartbeat\n\n"); err != nil {
103					return nil
104				}
105				if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
106					f.Flush()
107				}
108			}
109		}

143			duration := time.Until(next)
144	
145			timer := time.NewTimer(duration)

73		}
74	
75		if err := job.Validate(); err != nil {
76			return errors.Wrap(err, "invalid job")

94

97		}
98

125		handler := rj.job.Handler
126		if s.middleware != nil {
127			handler = s.middleware(handler)
128		}
129	
130		for {
131			// Calculate next run time
132			now := time.Now()
133			if rj.job.Timezone != "" {
134				loc, err := time.LoadLocation(rj.job.Timezone)
135				if err == nil {
136					now = now.In(loc)
137				}
138			} else if s.timezone != nil {
139				now = now.In(s.timezone)
140			}
141	
142			next := schedule.Next(now)
143			duration := time.Until(next)
144	
145			timer := time.NewTimer(duration)
146	
147			select {
148			case <-timer.C:
149				// Add job name to context and execute
150				jobCtx := withJobName(ctx, rj.job.Name)
151				if err := handler(jobCtx); err != nil {
152					// Error already handled by middleware (if any)
153					_ = err
154				}
155			case <-ctx.Done():
156				// Stop the timer to prevent it from firing. The timer will be garbage collected.
157				timer.Stop()
158				return
159			case <-s.stopCh:
160				// Stop the timer to prevent it from firing. The timer will be garbage collected.
161				timer.Stop()

170		s.runningMu.Lock()
171		if !s.running {
172			s.runningMu.Unlock()
173			return errors.New("scheduler not running")
174		}
175		s.running = false
176		s.runningMu.Unlock()
177

179		s.jobsMu.RLock()
180		for _, rj := range s.jobs {
181			if rj.cancelFn != nil {
182				rj.cancelFn()
183			}
184		}
185		s.jobsMu.RUnlock()
186	
187		// Signal stop and wait for jobs to finish
188		close(s.stopCh)
189	
190		done := make(chan struct{})
191		go func() {
192			s.wg.Wait()
193			close(done)
194		}()
195	
196		select {
197		case <-done:

**Delivery function:** `Post` (and its async wrapper `PostAsync`) — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (synchronous POST via `safeClient.Do(req)` at line 152); `PostAsync` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:184` enqueues onto `asyncPostQueue`, drained by worker goroutines started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`) that call `Post`.

**Protection mechanism:** `safeDialContext` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:59`, installed as the `DialContext` of the shared `safeClient`'s `http.Transport` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37`). It resolves the target host at dial time and rejects any resolved IP for which `isReservedIP` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:44`) returns true (loopback, RFC-1918 private, link-local/cloud IMDS, and IPv6 equivalents, per `reservedNetworks`/`reservedCIDRs` at `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-26`) — this dial-time check (as opposed to the one-time `ValidateURL` check at webhook creation/update, `internal/webhook/validate.go:62`, used in `server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go`) is what actually guards each outbound delivery and defeats DNS-rebinding.

36	// JSON returns the JSON representation of the event.

38	func (e *SSEEvent) JSON() []byte {
39		data, err := json.Marshal(e)
40		if err != nil {
41			slog.Error("failed to marshal SSE event", "err", err, "event", e)

49		events chan []byte
50		userID int32
51		role   store.Role
52	}
53	
54	// SSEHub manages SSE client connections and broadcasts events.
55	// It is safe for concurrent use.
56	type SSEHub struct {
57		mu      sync.RWMutex
58		clients map[*SSEClient]struct{}
59		closed  bool
60	}
61	
62	// NewSSEHub creates a new SSE hub.
63	func NewSSEHub() *SSEHub {
64		return &SSEHub{
65			clients: make(map[*SSEClient]struct{}),
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// Subscribe registers a new client and returns it.
70	// The caller must call Unsubscribe when done.
71	func (h *SSEHub) Subscribe(userID int32, role store.Role) *SSEClient {
72		c := &SSEClient{
73			// Buffer a few events so a slow client doesn't block broadcasting.
74			events: make(chan []byte, 32),
75			userID: userID,
76			role:   role,
77		}
78		h.mu.Lock()
79		if h.closed {
80			close(c.events)
81		} else {
82			h.clients[c] = struct{}{}
83		}
84		h.mu.Unlock()
85		return c
86	}
87	
88	// Unsubscribe removes a client and closes its channel.
89	func (h *SSEHub) Unsubscribe(c *SSEClient) {
90		h.mu.Lock()
91		if _, ok := h.clients[c]; ok {
92			delete(h.clients, c)
93			close(c.events)
94		}
95		h.mu.Unlock()
96	}
97	
98	// Close disconnects all subscribed SSE clients.
99	func (h *SSEHub) Close() {
100		h.mu.Lock()
101		defer h.mu.Unlock()
102		if h.closed {
103			return
104		}
105		h.closed = true
106		for c := range h.clients {
107			delete(h.clients, c)
108			close(c.events)
109		}
110	}
111	
112	// Broadcast sends an event to all connected clients.
113	// Slow clients that have a full buffer will have the event dropped
114	// to avoid blocking the broadcaster.
115	func (h *SSEHub) Broadcast(event *SSEEvent) {
116		data := event.JSON()
117		if len(data) == 0 {
118			return
119		}
120		h.mu.RLock()
121		defer h.mu.RUnlock()
122		for c := range h.clients {
123			if !c.canReceive(event) {
124				continue
125			}
126			select {
127			case c.events <- data:
128			default:
129				// Drop event for slow client to avoid blocking.
130			}
131		}
132	}

135		switch event.Visibility {
136		case store.Private:
137			return c.userID == event.CreatorID || c.role == store.RoleAdmin
138		case store.Public, store.Protected, "":
139			return true
140		default:
141			slog.Warn("SSE canReceive: unknown visibility type, denying event", "visibility", event.Visibility)
142			return false
143		}

h10. **`NewEngine`** — `internal/filter/engine.go:24` — approx **32 callers** (verified: `grep -c "NewEngine("` across the repo, cross-checked against CodeGraph's `calls` edges filtered to high-confidence/exact-match resolutions to exclude same-named-method noise like `sort.Interface.Len`/`io.Reader`-style collisions).

Most of the fan-in comes from test functions in `internal/filter/engine_test.go`, `internal/filter/functions_test.go`, and `internal/filter/time_test.go` (each constructing an engine via `NewEngine(NewSchema())` or `NewEngine(NewAttachmentSchema())` to exercise a filter-compilation case), plus 2 production call sites within `internal/filter/engine.go` itself (`DefaultEngine` and `DefaultAttachmentEngine`, which lazily build the package-wide singleton engines used across `store/db/*` and `server/router/api/v1/*` for memo/attachment filter compilation).

Note on methodology: a naive fan-in query over the CodeGraph SQLite index (`.codegraph/codegraph.db`) surfaces `SortVersion.Len` (`internal/version/version.go`) and `Schedule.Next` (`internal/scheduler/parser.go`) with much higher raw counts (180 and 57), but inspecting the edge `metadata` shows these are low-confidence (`confidence: 0.7`, `resolvedBy: "instance-method"`) name-only matches actually pointing at unrelated calls like `testify.assert.Len`, `bytes.Buffer.Len`, and `sql.Rows.Next` elsewhere in the codebase — not real calls to those internal/ symbols. Filtering to exact-match/qualified-name-resolved edges (or grep-verified call sites) removes that noise, leaving `NewEngine` as the legitimate top result.

h13.

**Impl:** the unexported `*markdown.service` struct (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:57-113`, wrapping a `goldmark.Markdown` instance) is the sole concrete implementation of the `markdown.Service` interface (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:31-55`) that runs at runtime — no other type implements it.

**Construction:** built exactly once via `markdown.NewService(markdown.WithTagExtension(), markdown.WithMentionExtension())` in `NewAPIV1Service` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51`), which configures goldmark with GFM plus the custom `#tag` and `@mention` extensions and auto heading IDs. That single instance is stored in `APIV1Service.MarkdownService`.

**Holders:**
- `APIV1Service.MarkdownService markdown.Service` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`) — the primary holder, constructed as above and used across memo creation/update/comment handling (`memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload`, snippet generation, etc.).
- `RSSService.MarkdownService markdown.Service` (`server/router/rss/rss.go:45`) — receives the *same* instance, wired at server startup: `rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService).RegisterRoutes(rootGroup)` (`server/server.go:85`); used for `RenderHTML` when generating RSS feed content (`server/router/rss/rss.go:339`).
- `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService markdown.Service` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16`) — declares the field and accepts it via `NewRunner(store, markdownService)`, but (per prior analysis of this codebase) `memopayload.NewRunner`/`Runner` is never constructed anywhere in production code — only the package-level `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` function is called directly (from `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108,447`), passing `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` as the argument. So this third holder exists in source but is dead at runtime.

(The standalone `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce`, `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27-72`, would bulk-recompute this for every memo, but per earlier analysis it is never constructed/invoked in production — only `RebuildMemoPayload` itself is used, directly from the two call sites above.)

**Extracted properties** (per `ExtractedData`, `internal/markdown/markdown.go:21-25`, and `storepb.MemoPayload_Property`, `proto/gen/store/memo.pb.go:85-95`):
- `Tags` — all `#tag` nodes found in the content (deduplicated, case-preserved).
- `Mentions` — all `@mention` usernames found (lowercased, deduplicated) — used elsewhere for mention notifications, not stored directly in `Property`.
- `Property.Title` — text of the first H1 heading, if the document's first block-level child is one.
- `Property.HasLink` — true if any link node is present.
- `Property.HasCode` — true if any code block/fenced code block/code span is present.
- `Property.HasTaskList` — true if any task checkbox is present.
- `Property.HasIncompleteTasks` — true if any task checkbox is unchecked.

651		// For unlinked attachments, only the creator can access.
652		if attachment.MemoID == nil {
653			user, err := s.getCurrentUser(ctx, c)
654			if err != nil {
655				return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to get current user").Wrap(err)
656			}
657			if user == nil {
658				return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized access")
659			}
660			if user.ID != attachment.CreatorID && user.Role != store.RoleAdmin {
661				return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusForbidden, "forbidden access")
662			}
663			return nil
664		}
665	
666		memo, err := s.Store.GetMemo(ctx, &store.FindMemo{ID: attachment.MemoID})
667		if err != nil {
668			return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to find memo").Wrap(err)
669		}
670		if memo == nil {
671			return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusNotFound, "memo not found")
672		}
673	
674		// Public-visibility attachments are served to anonymous visitors only when the
675		// instance allows anonymous access. On a private instance (no InstanceURL), the
676		// request must still resolve to an authenticated user or a valid share token below.
677		if memo.Visibility == store.Public && s.Profile.AllowAnonymous() {
678			return nil
679		}
680	
681		// Check share token fallback: allow access if request carries a valid, non-expired share token
682		// that was issued for this specific memo. This covers attachment requests made from the shared
683		// memo page for private or protected memos.
684		if shareToken := (*c).QueryParam("share_token"); shareToken != "" {
685			ms, err := s.Store.GetMemoShare(ctx, &store.FindMemoShare{UID: &shareToken})
686			if err == nil && ms != nil && !isMemoShareExpired(ms) && ms.MemoID == memo.ID {
687				return nil
688			}
689		}
690	
691		user, err := s.getCurrentUser(ctx, c)
692		if err != nil {
693			return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to get current user").Wrap(err)
694		}
695		if user == nil {
696			return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized access")
697		}
698	
699		if memo.Visibility == store.Private && user.ID != memo.CreatorID && user.Role != store.RoleAdmin {

701		}

651		// For unlinked attachments, only the creator can access.

654			if err != nil {

656			}
657			if user == nil {
658				return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized access")
659			}
660			if user.ID != attachment.CreatorID && user.Role != store.RoleAdmin {
661				return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusForbidden, "forbidden access")
662			}
663			return nil
664		}
665	
666		memo, err := s.Store.GetMemo(ctx, &store.FindMemo{ID: attachment.MemoID})
667		if err != nil {
668			return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to find memo").Wrap(err)
669		}
670		if memo == nil {
671			return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusNotFound, "memo not found")
672		}
673	
674		// Public-visibility attachments are served to anonymous visitors only when the
675		// instance allows anonymous access. On a private instance (no InstanceURL), the
676		// request must still resolve to an authenticated user or a valid share token below.
677		if memo.Visibility == store.Public && s.Profile.AllowAnonymous() {
678			return nil
679		}
680	
681		// Check share token fallback: allow access if request carries a valid, non-expired share token
682		// that was issued for this specific memo. This covers attachment requests made from the shared
683		// memo page for private or protected memos.
684		if shareToken := (*c).QueryParam("share_token"); shareToken != "" {
685			ms, err := s.Store.GetMemoShare(ctx, &store.FindMemoShare{UID: &shareToken})
686			if err == nil && ms != nil && !isMemoShareExpired(ms) && ms.MemoID == memo.ID {
687				return nil
688			}
689		}
690	
691		user, err := s.getCurrentUser(ctx, c)
692		if err != nil {
693			return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to get current user").Wrap(err)
694		}
695		if user == nil {
696			return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized access")
697		}
698	
699		if memo.Visibility == store.Private && user.ID != memo.CreatorID && user.Role != store.RoleAdmin {

r01.

**Premise correction:** There is no Redis anywhere in this codebase — `grep -rli "redis" --include="*.go" .` returns zero hits. The repo has no Redis client dependency (not in `go.mod`) and no Redis connection configuration exists.

**Actual mechanism:** Caching is done entirely in-process via `store/cache/cache.go` — a thread-safe in-memory `Cache` (backed by `sync.Map` with a background cleanup goroutine, `store/cache/cache.go:66-90`). `store.Store` constructs three of these in-memory caches in `store/store.go:38-61` (`instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`), each configured with:

```go
cacheConfig := cache.Config{
    DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
    CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
    MaxItems:        1000,
    OnEviction:      nil,
}
```

So the **user entries TTL is 10 minutes** (`DefaultTTL`, `store/store.go:41`), with expired entries swept by a cleanup goroutine every 5 minutes (`CleanupInterval`) and a 1000-item cap per cache (`MaxItems`) — all enforced by `store/cache/cache.go` (`SetWithTTL`/`cleanupLoop`/`cleanupOldest`), not by any external Redis instance.

Neither implements request throttling or per-user limits. Some individual subsystems have their own local concurrency caps (not rate limits) — e.g. `thumbnailSemaphore`/`imageProcessingSemaphore` in `APIV1Service` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:39-41`) bound concurrent thumbnail/image work, and the webhook dispatch queue is a bounded channel (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`) — but none of these enforce a per-user request-rate limit on the API surface.

**Actual mechanism:** The only two production background jobs (`server/server.go:153-174`, `startBackgroundRunners`) are plain `time.Ticker`-driven goroutines, not registered with the cron `Scheduler`:
- `s3presign.Runner.Run` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:29-41`) — re-presigns S3 attachment URLs every 12 hours (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`).

A `grep` for `cleanup`/`purge`/`vacuum` across the Go backend turns up only unrelated code: in-memory cache eviction (`store/cache/cache.go`), attachment/storage cleanup helper functions invoked synchronously from request handlers (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, `user_service.go`, `store/attachment.go`), and `store/store.go`'s `Close()` shutting down cache goroutines — none of these are cron-scheduled or database-wide cleanup jobs.

**Actual mechanism:** Webhook delivery workers consume from an in-process, in-memory Go channel, not a broker. In `internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`:

```go
asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)
```

`init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`) spawns 4 goroutines that range over `asyncPostQueue`, calling `Post` for each payload. `PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184-196`) enqueues onto this channel (non-blockingly dropping and logging a warning if the buffer of 128 is full). This queue lives only in the process's memory — it is not durable, not shared across instances, and has no broker connection to declare.

r05.

**Premise correction:** There is no GraphQL API in this repository — `grep -rli "graphql"` across all Go files returns nothing, and there are no `.graphql`/`.gql` schema files anywhere in the codebase.

**Actual API surface:** The public API is defined via Protobuf and served through gRPC + Connect + a gRPC-Gateway REST translation layer:
- Schema source: `.proto` files under `proto/` (e.g. `proto/api/v1/*.proto` — memo, user, attachment, auth, idp, ai, shortcut services), compiled into `proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.go`.
- Server wiring: `APIV1Service` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go`) implements the generated `*ServiceServer`/`*ServiceHandler` interfaces for each service.
- `RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go` / called from `server/server.go:88`) registers both the gRPC-Gateway (REST/JSON over HTTP, via `proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.gw.go`) and Connect handlers (`proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/*.connect.go`, wired in `server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go` / `connect_services.go`) on the same Echo server.
- There's additionally an MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool surface auto-derived from an OpenAPI-style schema (`server/router/mcp/openapi.go`, `catalog.go`) — also not GraphQL, but worth noting since it's the only other schema-driven API layer in the repo.
